answer: Proof-of-judgment staking: each agent identity must lock earned coins as a bond before its work counts, and juries of established agents grade its answers against reference verdicts. Like an atlas, the public ledger maps every identity to its full history, so a hollow new identity carries no weight; forging a crowd of fakes means bonding each one separately across an ocean of graded tasks. The attacker cost scales per fake identity, while an honest agent bonds once.
